Four Astra specialists across low, medium and high reasoning, plus independent review and primary-agent synthesis.

Comprehensive repository assessment · 5 September 2026

A lean foundation.
Correctness needs another pass.

ScreenMark’s core/editor separation is sound, and its existing checks pass. The highest-priority defect is destructive budget regeneration. Export fidelity and editor behavior also have reproducible gaps that the current tests miss.

47 / 47project files covered
46 / 46existing tests pass · Bun & Node
28findings and review observations
1 high15 medium · 12 low

Baseline: 1,746 filesystem entries outside internal Git metadata, including 1,699 dependency files/links. The 1,378 VSIX members were inventoried separately. Dependency content received integrity/metadata and targeted runtime review; this report does not claim manual source review of every third-party line.

Fix before the next release: protect user budget data.

Budget Summary can pair an ordinary earlier ## Totals heading with a later generated closing marker, deleting the source rows between them. See CORE-001. The first refresh may still display the old total, hiding the loss until the next refresh.

What is working

  • Compact, explicit AST and parser; 1,768 source lines across 14 TypeScript modules.
  • Core logic has no VS Code imports; editor providers are kept in small modules.
  • Type checking and reproducible bundling pass. All 46 existing tests pass under both Bun and Node.
  • HTML text escaping, nonce-based CSP and per-call PDF state hold up in the exercised cases.
  • The VSIX runtime matches current source output and includes required PDFKit font assets.

Where confidence is missing

  • Financial edits need explicit generated-region ownership and input validation.
  • PDF tests miss text clipping, unsupported glyphs, empty documents and interacting pagination rules.
  • Editor features have no real-host integration tests; mock tests expose lifecycle and edit-range bugs.
  • Exact-page and complete-cast claims exceed what current planning calculations provide.
  • Release tooling, sample artifacts and packaged documentation are not kept in one verified release step.
02 / Macro review

Architecture and boundaries

ScreenMark text
Simple frontmatter
Line-oriented syntax
Notes and production tags
→
Parser + AST
Discriminated unions
Source line positions
Dialogue state
→
Outputs + host adapter
PDF / HTML / Fountain
Breakdown → schedule
VS Code commands, views, edits

The current module boundaries are appropriate for a small extension. Keep them. Most defects come from a representation losing information or a state transition crossing boundaries: stripped comments lose original offsets, per-scene layout loses global spacing, a pending preview callback outlives its document selection, and totals replacement loses ownership boundaries.

BoundaryAssessmentSmallest useful improvement
Text → ASTThe parser is the semantic authority, but scene numbering rescans text independently. Comment stripping preserves lines while discarding columns and comment provenance.Drive numbering from parsed scenes and retain enough offset information to edit safely. Specify comment-only dialogue behavior.
AST → PDF layoutGeometry is explicit and easy to inspect. Single-line spans and local keep counts cannot represent all wrapping/pagination interactions.Wrap all printable element types and keep the first content group with its scene. Skip structural elements without popping preceding layout state.
Layout → planningReusing layout is a good instinct, but breakdown lays out each scene separately and copies the 54-line geometry constant.Define occupied eighths precisely; derive scene spans from the full layout and keep shared geometry in one existing boundary.
Editor events → previewOne stable HTML shell and a ready handshake avoid reload storms. A timer can restore a stale document.Cancel or invalidate pending work when tracked document changes. Avoid broader state-management machinery.
Workbook → editIn-place generated totals are convenient and undoable, but heading matching alone does not establish ownership.Bound owned regions to the same section and leave unowned content intact. Detect invalid nonempty amounts.
Package → hostExternal PDFKit preserves font lookup, and workspace.fs/URI APIs support host filesystems. The entry eagerly imports PDFKit; no browser entry is supplied.Keep desktop/remote-host scope explicit. Validate the minimum supported VS Code and current Cursor in an installed-package smoke test before changing the architecture.

No database, server, authentication layer, telemetry service, network API or deployment configuration exists in the reviewed application. Introducing those layers would not solve the observed defects.

03 / Micro review

Prioritized findings

Severity reflects this project’s impact, not a CVSS score. High means user data loss; medium means broken output or workflow; low covers limited edge cases, ambiguous behavior and release hygiene. Reproduction and static verification are labeled separately.

high CORE-001 Reproduced

Budget totals replacement can delete source budget sections and producer notes

A normal in-place Budget Summary can remove user-authored financial source data when an earlier Totals heading exists. Undo may recover it, but the function violates its promise to leave everything else untouched.

src/core/budget.ts:134 · src/core/budget.ts:139 · src/core/budget.ts:156 · test/budget.test.ts:62

Evidence, remediation and verification
Evidence / trigger
upsertTotals searches for the first exact ## Totals heading, then takes the first GENERATED_END anywhere later in the entire document. Reproduction prepends an ordinary ## Totals / Producer notes: KEEP THIS section before a production budget with an existing generated totals block. Refresh deletes the notes, ## Production, and the $1,000 Crew input row. The remaining generated table initially says $1,000; parseBudget then returns zero, and the next refresh replaces its amounts with $0.
Recommended change
Identify a generated block by an owned start marker and an end sentinel bounded to the same section. Do not pair an arbitrary Totals heading with a distant sentinel across prose or headings. Preserve unowned sections and test duplicate/unowned Totals headings.
Verification / limits
bun /tmp/screenmark-core-repro.ts; bun /tmp/screenmark-core-audit-build.ts. before/after evidence in /tmp/screenmark-core-repro-results.json at totalsDataLoss.

medium CORE-002 Reproduced

Escaped Markdown pipes silently shift budget amounts into the wrong columns

Users can get incorrect financial totals from a correctly escaped Markdown item name, without an error or warning.

src/core/budget.ts:33 · src/core/budget.ts:37 · src/core/budget.ts:80 · test/budget.test.ts:21

Evidence, remediation and verification
Evidence / trigger
The valid Markdown row | Camera \| lens | 100 | 120 | kit | is split at every pipe. The parsed item becomes Camera \, estimate becomes null, actual becomes 100, and notes becomes 120. Generated totals report $0 estimate / $100 actual instead of $100 / $120.
Recommended change
Split Markdown table rows while respecting escaped pipes, and validate row width and invalid nonempty amount cells so malformed rows cannot silently become zero-cost entries.
Verification / limits
Results escapedBudgetPipe; focused assertions confirm estimate 0 and actual 100 for a 100/120 input.

medium CORE-004 Static / contract verified

Fountain export does not preserve all explicitly parsed action and character types

The exported screenplay can change scene structure, misformat dialogue, or replace printed action with nonprinting control syntax when opened in Fountain software.

src/core/fountain.ts:44 · src/core/fountain.ts:49 · src/core/fountain.ts:54 · src/core/fountain.ts:55 · test/fountain.test.ts:36

Evidence, remediation and verification
Evidence / trigger
Parsed actions "INT. A camera label reads wide angle.", ".a small red dot", "> a stray quote", and "===" are emitted unchanged; Fountain syntax classifies these as a scene heading, forced scene heading, transition, and page break respectively. The valid ScreenMark cue **23** is emitted as 23 without @, although Fountain requires at least one alphabetic character for automatic character recognition.
Recommended change
Force action paragraphs when their first line conflicts with any Fountain block syntax, and force character cues unless they satisfy the full Fountain character-recognition rules. Verify semantic types against a Fountain parser or comprehensive syntax fixtures.
Verification / limits
Results fountainAction/numericCue contain source AST and emitted text. Semantic classifications checked against the primary Fountain syntax reference https://fountain.io/syntax/ (Action, Scene Headings, Character, Transition, Page Breaks); no third-party importer was executed.

medium CORE-007 Reproduced

Scene-length estimates omit interscene rows from the full PDF layout

Scene eighths are computed from isolated layouts and rounded per scene, so they do not precisely represent full-document layout. Scheduling inherits these estimates. The fixture yields 12.5 estimated pages versus 798/54 = 14.78 occupied-row pages and 15 physical pages; rounded occupied length and physical page count are different quantities; the sample alone does not prove a systematic scheduling shortfall.

src/core/breakdown.ts:95 · src/core/breakdown.ts:96 · src/core/breakdown.ts:103 · src/core/schedule.ts:24

Evidence, remediation and verification
Evidence / trigger
100 scenes, each containing a heading and the four separate action lines One./Two./Three./Four., produce 100 eighths (12.5 pages) from buildBreakdown, but layout(parse(fullScript)) contains 798 rows and paginate returns 15 printed pages. Each scene is laid out independently, so the two interscene separator rows inserted by the full-document layout are absent from the scene measurements.
Recommended change
Define whether eighths measure occupied screenplay length or physical printed page spans, then measure scene ranges from the full-document layout and apply a documented rounding rule. Add a many-short-scenes comparison against full layout; do not claim exact printed correspondence for independent rounded scene lengths.
Verification / limits
Results pageEstimate: scenes=100, totalEighths=100, estimatedPages=12.5, printedPages=15, layoutLines=798; focused assertions passed.

medium EXPORT-01 Reproduced

A pending preview debounce switches tracking back to the previous document

Normal fast tab switching leaves the preview showing the wrong screenplay and permanently stops live updates for the active file until another activation event occurs.

src/features/preview.ts:78 · src/features/preview.ts:88

Evidence, remediation and verification
Evidence / trigger
The scheduled callback closes over the edited document, while update() does not cancel that timer when the active document changes. Bun mock reproduction: edit A, activate B before 300 ms, observe Preview: B.smark immediately, then Preview: A.smark after 350 ms. Render sequence is A, B, A. Editing the still-active B afterwards produces no render because trackedDoc has reverted to A.
Recommended change
Cancel any pending debounce when changing the tracked document, or reject callbacks whose document/generation is no longer current; cover edit A -> switch B -> timer fires -> edit B.
Verification / limits
bun /tmp/screenmark-export-audit/preview-repro.ts; observed immediate B, delayed A, subsequent B edit ignored. Uses a VS Code API mock, not a running extension host.

medium EXPORT-03 Reproduced

Scene headings can be orphaned when the following dialogue cue moves pages

A scene heading is printed at the bottom of one page without any scene content, breaking the intended screenplay pagination rule.

src/core/pdf.ts:174 · src/core/pdf.ts:235

Evidence, remediation and verification
Evidence / trigger
A scene uses keepWithNext: 2, which counts the blank and cue but not the cue's own keep requirement. With 49 newline-separated action lines followed by a scene heading and one-line MAYA dialogue, page 1 ends ['Filler 48', '', '', 'INT. ROOM - DAY', '']; page 2 contains ['MAYA', 'Hello.']. The local lookahead passes the scene, then flushes at the cue.
Recommended change
Compute transitive keep groups for a scene plus the first printable content, including a dialogue cue and at least one body line. Add boundary tests for scene->action and scene->dialogue.
Verification / limits
bun /tmp/screenmark-export-audit/repro.ts prints scene-orphan with page lengths 53 and 2 and the isolated heading on page 1.

medium EXPORT-04 Reproduced

Long headings and other unwrapped spans print beyond the PDF page

Valid screenplay text is silently lost in print; long locations/cues or title metadata can overlap other fields and gutters. Preview and PDF disagree because the HTML can wrap these blocks.

src/core/pdf.ts:169 · src/core/pdf.ts:201 · src/core/pdf.ts:267 · src/core/pdf.ts:316

Evidence, remediation and verification
Evidence / trigger
Scene headings, cues, transitions, centered text and title fields are emitted as single spans. Rendering disables PDFKit wrapping with lineBreak:false. A valid heading containing 'VERY LONG LOCATION ' repeated five times clips at the right page edge and overprints its right scene number; centered text repeated seven times clips too. The missing heading suffix '- DAY' never appears in pdftotext's visible-page extraction. Render inspected at /tmp/screenmark-export-audit/overflow-1.png.
Recommended change
Wrap every potentially long text-bearing element to its available width, reserve the numbered-scene gutter, and reflect wrapped row counts in pagination and keep groups. Handle title-page fields with bounded widths.

medium EXPORT-05 Reproduced

Built-in Courier silently corrupts non-Latin screenplay text

Multilingual dialogue, names and emoji can produce a successful-looking export with corrupted content, despite displaying correctly in the source and HTML preview.

src/core/pdf.ts:36 · src/core/pdf.ts:316

Evidence, remediation and verification
Evidence / trigger
Exporting '你好世界. Привет мир. Ελληνικά. café naïve — “quotes” 👋.' renders nonsensical Latin glyphs instead of the original text; in this mixed string subsequent Latin text is corrupted too. The installed PDFKit built-in font path uses WinAnsiEncoding and encodeText() hex encodes unsupported codepoints without a Unicode font. Visually inspected /tmp/screenmark-export-audit/unicode-1.png; pdftotext shows garbage rather than the supplied text.
Recommended change
Use an embedded monospaced font with the supported script coverage and correct Unicode shaping/measurement, or explicitly detect and reject unsupported glyphs rather than silently exporting corrupt text. Add mixed-script extraction/render checks.
Verification / limits
bun /tmp/screenmark-export-audit/repro.ts writes unicode.pdf; pdftotext -layout /tmp/screenmark-export-audit/unicode.pdf - and rendered unicode-1.png both confirm corruption.

medium EXT-01 Reproduced

Number Scenes writes the number inside a multiline note and never numbers the scene

A valid scene heading with an inline multiline production note remains unnumbered, breaking the promised persistent identifiers used by reports. Repeating the command silently changes note content.

src/extension.ts:88

Evidence, remediation and verification
Evidence / trigger
The scan uses note-stripped text, but the insertion uses the original line end (lines 66–89). Executing the actual registered command against `## INT. ROOM - DAY <!-- note\nrest -->` produced `## INT. ROOM - DAY <!-- note #1#\nrest -->`; parsing still reports number=undefined. A second invocation appends another #1# inside the same note.
Recommended change
Use parsed scene elements for eligibility and place the number before a trailing note opener when the original line ends within a note. Preserve original offsets while stripping notes rather than assuming the original line end is syntactically available.
Verification / limits

Tests that would change confidence

Prioritize regression fixtures for confirmed failures, then one installed-extension smoke flow: open a script, accept a character completion with auto-closing enabled, number a commented scene, switch previews while editing, export PDF/Fountain, generate planning files, and safely refresh a budget. Run it in the declared minimum VS Code and a supported current host. A much larger unit-test count alone would not cover these boundaries.

There are no first-party HTML/preview/provider tests, no imported Fountain semantic comparison and no release-host test in the baseline. The existing PDF “short dialogue near page bottom” test constructs the wrong boundary (EXPORT-07). Coverage percentages were not measured, and passing unit tests should not be read as complete product verification.

05 / Trust and supply chain

Security and dependency posture

Application trust boundaries

Source text becomes escaped HTML text, numeric line attributes and PDF/Fountain/report content. The preview uses a random 16-byte nonce and a default-deny CSP; no unescaped parser-controlled HTML path or privileged inbound webview command was demonstrated.

CSV output prefixes the common formula starters = + - @ and quotes commas, quotes and newlines. Spreadsheet application behavior for other control-character cases was not tested. Arbitrary tag dictionary keys can still trigger a local availability failure.

Commands write sibling exports or a workbook through VS Code’s filesystem APIs. The budget ownership error is the material integrity issue. No shell execution, remote endpoint, credential store or application telemetry path was found in first-party source.

Dependency evidence

There is one declared runtime dependency: PDFKit 0.15.2, bringing 79 installed production packages including itself. All 89 installed production/development package versions match their lock entries. The lock also contains optional-platform records: 137 total entries.

All locked entries have HTTPS npm registry URLs and integrity fields. The inspected package license metadata is mostly MIT; png-js lacks a license field but contains an MIT LICENSE file. Required runtime font files and notices are included. No complete license-compatibility opinion or live vulnerability clearance is claimed.

The old esbuild CORS advisory applies to an unused development-server path (DEP-01). Two newer maintainer advisories were screened: the Windows server advisory lists 0.27.3, and the Deno downloader advisory concerns a Deno path absent here.

Sources: esbuild CORS advisory, Windows development-server advisory, Deno downloader advisory. Read 5 September 2026. These targeted checks are not a complete advisory scan of the dependency graph.

06 / End-to-end behavior

Product, usability and scale

AreaCurrent statePractical consequence
AuthoringReadable small dialect; useful snippets, outline and sidebar. Frontmatter is simple single-line key/value parsing, not full YAML. Literal Markdown styling is generally preserved as text.Document the dialect’s limits and make completion/comment behavior consistent with parser semantics. No general Markdown engine is needed.
PlanningCast comes exclusively from dialogue cues; silent action performers are omitted. NIGHT/DUSK/EVENING/MIDNIGHT use exact matching; LATER/CONTINUOUS do not infer context.Label this as speaking cast and a draft schedule. The sample itself shows silent performers in scenes with empty Cast cells. This cannot yet serve as a complete call list.
BudgetManual USD-style amounts and fixed section tables; contingency is a label, not a computed percentage. Invalid nonempty amounts silently become null/zero; multiple differently shaped tables in one section are not robustly modeled.Validate nonempty amount cells and document one-table-per-section expectations. Prioritize preservation and precise arithmetic over adding more financial features.
Preview accessibilityText-based output inherits host styling; headings are generic divs and scene numbers sit outside the main column. No keyboard/screen-reader or narrow-webview check was executed.Screen-reader structure and narrow-panel clipping remain verification gaps; do not claim an accessibility conformance result.
Workspace supportURI components are retained for sibling files. Init Budget chooses the first root. Exports from untitled/virtual documents and external opening of remote PDFs were not host-tested.Fix the reproduced root-selection bug; explicitly test writable virtual/remote URIs before advertising wider filesystem support.
ResponsivenessParsing, PDF layout and breakdown computation run synchronously in the extension host; text preview replaces body HTML after debounce. Project tree probes up to five siblings sequentially per script.Normal measured PDF work is fast. Large tagged scripts and slow filesystem providers warrant bounded measurements before introducing caches or workers.

Measured stress behavior

One warmed measurement per synthetic size shows repeated prefix scanning and scene-array reversal in collectTags. These inputs are intentionally much larger than a typical screenplay; the figures describe this machine and fixture, not a general latency guarantee.

ScenesTagged input bytesWith one note per sceneSame scenes without notes
1,00057,77835.4 ms
1.5 ms
2,000117,778128.1 ms
2.8 ms
4,000237,778805.4 ms
21.2 ms
8,000477,7781,955.9 ms
10.3 ms

By contrast, a 6,000-line / 112-page synthetic PDF completed in about 59 ms; four concurrent exports completed independently in about 23 ms total. The targeted improvement for tag-heavy inputs is a single advancing source-line/scene cursor. There is no measured reason here to introduce workers for ordinary PDF export.

07 / Actionable order

Recommended remediation sequence

OrderConcrete workAcceptance evidence
1 · Preserve dataBound generated totals ownership; parse escaped table pipes; detect invalid nonempty amounts; normalize monetary precision.Duplicate/unowned Totals, distant sentinel, trailing notes, escaped item pipes and equal-cent sums remain correct and idempotent.
2 · Preserve screenplay outputHandle unwrapped spans, Unicode support/failure, empty exports, explicit breaks after sections, transitive scene/dialogue keeps and Fountain control collisions.Extracted text matches supported source text; rendered boundary fixtures have no clipping/orphans; valid pages are emitted; Fountain types survive a semantic import check.
3 · Fix editor state and editsInvalidate stale preview timers, number parser-confirmed scenes outside comments, respect active workspace, correct completion filtering/replacement.Run the mock regressions plus a real extension-host flow with auto-closing and rapid tab switches.
4 · Define planning contractsUse safe tag storage, escape Markdown fields, document speaking cast and occupied eighths, measure scene ranges consistently.Adversarial tag keys and delimiters work; full-layout comparison uses a documented rounding rule; sample reports clearly reflect the intended contract.
5 · Verify a coherent releasePin packager, align Bun scripts, enforce checks, sync metadata/docs/samples, prune verified-unused package content and exclude audit reports.Fresh packaged extension passes a host smoke test; all code examples remain intact; runtime assets/notices remain; package contents and versioned docs agree.

This sequence is a recommendation, not an implementation plan already approved for source changes. No fixes, commits, pushes, installations of the extension, publishing or deployments were performed.

SHA-256 8f40a2f7b9868a6763984a1cd4b2a837d70ea025b846e3978e97e2b66f081971
Reviewed source snapshot

   4  
   5  # ScreenMark
   6  
   7  **Write screenplays in markdown. Export real screenplay PDFs — then plan the shoot.**
   8  
   9  For Cursor and VS Code.
  10  
  11  </div>
  12  
  13  ![ScreenMark editor and live preview](media/screenshots/hero.png)
  14  
  15  ## Why
  16  
  17  Screenwriting apps lock your script in their format. ScreenMark keeps it in plain markdown you already know, in the editor you already use, under version control — and still gives you a correctly formatted PDF.
  18  
  19  Then it goes further: your script is structured data, so ScreenMark reads it back to build scene breakdowns, shooting schedules, and budgets.
  20  
  21  ## Write
  22  
  23  ````markdown
  24  ---
  25  title: Cold Brew
  26  credit: written by
  27  author: Your Name
  28  ---
  29  
  30  ## INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY #1#
  31  
  32  Maya wipes down the counter, eyeing the door.
  33  
  34  **MAYA**
  35  _(under her breath)_
  36  > He's late. Again.
  37  
  38  @CUT TO:
  39  ````
  40  
  41  Files are `.smark` or `*.screen.md` — the `.md` flavor still renders fine on GitHub.
  42  
  43  | Element | Syntax |
  44  |---|---|
  45  | Title page | frontmatter: `title`, `credit`, `author`, `draft`, `date`, `contact` |
  46  | Act / section | `# ACT ONE` — outline only, never printed |
  47  | Scene heading | `## INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY` |
  48  | Scene number | trailing `#4A#` — prints in both margins |
  49  | Action | plain paragraphs |
  50  | Character | `**MAYA**` on its own line (`**MAYA (V.O.)**` works) |
  51  | Parenthetical | `_(under her breath)_` |
  52  | Dialog | `> ` lines under a character |
  53  | Dual dialog | `**JONAS** ^` — prints side by side |
  54  | Lyric | `~ sung line` |
  55  | Transition | `@CUT TO:` |
  56  | Centered | `> THE END <` |
  57  | Page break | `---` |
  58  | Note | `<!-- fix pacing -->` — never printed |
  59  
  60  A blank line ends a dialog block.
  61  
  62  **Editor help:** syntax highlighting, character/scene/transition autocomplete, scene outline, folding, and snippets (`title`, `scene`, `dialog`, `dual`, `trans`).
  63  
  64  ## The ScreenMark sidebar
  65  
  66  Click the clapperboard in the Activity Bar for one-click access to everything — no command palette needed.
  67  
  68  <img src="media/screenshots/sidebar.png" width="300" alt="ScreenMark sidebar">
  69  
  70  **Actions** groups every command by task; **Film Project** lists your scripts with their generated docs. The two most-used actions — Open Preview and Export PDF — also sit in the editor's title bar toolbar.
  71  
  72  ## Export
  73  
  74  | Command | Result |
  75  |---|---|
  76  | **Export PDF** | US Letter, Courier 12pt, industry margins, title page, `(MORE)`/`(CONT'D)`, dual-dialog columns |
  77  | **Export Fountain** | standard `.fountain` for Highland, Slugline, Final Draft |
  78  | **Open Preview** | live formatted preview that follows your scroll |
  79  | **Number Scenes** | fills in missing `#n#`, never renumbers existing ones |
  80  
  81  <img src="media/screenshots/pdf.png" width="380" alt="Exported screenplay PDF">
  82  
  83  ## Plan the shoot
  84  
  85  Tag production elements inside any note:
  86  
  87  ```markdown
  88  <!-- @prop: revolver, whiskey glass @wardrobe: red coat @vfx: muzzle flash -->
  89  ```
  90  
  91  **Scene Breakdown** turns the script into a report (`.md` + `.csv`) — location, time, cast, tagged elements, and page length in eighths measured off the real PDF layout.
  92  
  93  ![Scene breakdown report](media/screenshots/breakdown.png)
  94  
  95  **Shooting Schedule** packs scenes into days: grouped by location to cut company moves, day work before night, sized by `screenmark.pagesPerDay` (default 5).
  96  
  97  ![Shooting schedule](media/screenshots/schedule.png)
  98  
  99  **Init Budget** scaffolds `budget.md`; **Budget Summary** recomputes totals and over/under variance in place. The **Film Project** panel in the Explorer keeps every script, report, and budget one click away.
 100  
 101  Scene numbers are the glue — number once, and every report keeps pointing at the same scene as the script moves around.
 102  
 103  ## Install
 104  
 105  Grab the `.vsix` from [Releases](../../releases) and:
 106  
 107  ```bash
 108  cursor --install-extension screen-mark-0.2.1.vsix   # or: code --install-extension ...
 109  ```
 110  
 111  ## Develop
 112  
 113  ```bash
 114  npm install
 115  npm test          # 46 tests: parser, fountain, pdf, breakdown, budget
 116  npm run build
 117  npm run package   # → .vsix
 118  ```
 119  
 120  Press <kbd>F5</kbd> to launch a dev host with the sample script open.
 121  
 122  Everything that parses and renders lives in `src/core/` with no `vscode` imports, so it can move to a CLI or web tool unchanged. `src/features/` holds the editor integration.
 123  
 124  ## Roadmap
 125  
 126  Call sheets, cast day-out-of-days, and budget estimates seeded from the breakdown.
 127  
 128  ## License
 129  
 130  MIT

src/core/breakdown.ts — Source / config / document review · 6,234 bytes

Reviewed scene slicing, slug interpretation, cast normalization, tag association, layout-based eighths, aggregation, CSV defense, and Markdown output. Reproduced CORE-003, CORE-005, and CORE-007. CSV protects common =,+,-,@ starters and quotes commas/quotes/newlines. Tags bind to the nearest preceding source scene. Limitation: cast is speaking cues only; silent performers are not inferred or explicitly integrated into cast. SHA-256 750b2a9b84cda915d638244aa7d8049a5770a9ccc1b7327b606632d808832eb5
Reviewed source snapshot
   1  import { SceneHeading } from './ast';
   2  import { parse } from './parser';
   3  import { layout } from './pdf';
   4  
   5  export interface SceneBreakdown {
   6    /** Stable scene ID from `#4A#`, if assigned. */
   7    number?: string;
   8    slug: string;
   9    intExt: 'INT' | 'EXT' | 'INT/EXT' | 'OTHER';
  10    location: string;
  11    timeOfDay: string;
  12    characters: string[];
  13    /** Scene length in eighths of a page (industry scheduling unit), minimum 1. */
  14    eighths: number;
  15    /** Production elements tagged in notes, e.g. { prop: ['revolver'], vfx: [...] }. */
  16    tags: Record<string, string[]>;
  17    line: number;
  18  }
  19  
  20  export interface Breakdown {
  21    scenes: SceneBreakdown[];
  22    characters: string[];
  23    locations: string[];
  24    totalEighths: number;
  25  }
  26  
  27  const SLUG_RE = /^(INT\.?\/EXT\.?|I\/E|INT|EXT|EST)[.\s]+(.*)$/i;
  28  // Same page geometry as pdf.ts: 54 lines per page.
  29  const LINES_PER_EIGHTH = 54 / 8;
  30  
  31  export function formatEighths(eighths: number): string {
  32    const whole = Math.floor(eighths / 8);
  33    const rem = eighths % 8;
  34    if (whole && rem) return `${whole} ${rem}/8`;
  35    if (whole) return `${whole}`;
  36    return `${rem}/8`;
  37  }
  38  
  39  function parseSlug(text: string): Pick<SceneBreakdown, 'intExt' | 'location' | 'timeOfDay'> {
  40    const m = text.match(SLUG_RE);
  41    if (!m) return { intExt: 'OTHER', location: text.toUpperCase(), timeOfDay: '' };
  42    const prefix = m[1].toUpperCase();
  43    const intExt = prefix.includes('/') ? 'INT/EXT' : prefix === 'EST' ? 'EXT' : (prefix as 'INT' | 'EXT');
  44    const segs = m[2].split(/\s+-\s+/);
  45    if (segs.length > 1) {
  46      return {
  47        intExt,
  48        location: segs.slice(0, -1).join(' - ').toUpperCase().trim(),
  49        timeOfDay: segs[segs.length - 1].toUpperCase().trim(),
  50      };
  51    }
  52    return { intExt, location: m[2].toUpperCase().trim(), timeOfDay: '' };
  53  }
  54  
  55  /** Attach `@category: item, item` tags found in <!-- --> notes to the scene containing them. */
  56  function collectTags(text: string, scenes: SceneBreakdown[]): void {
  57    const noteRe = /<!--([\s\S]*?)(?:-->|$)/g; // unclosed note runs to EOF, matching stripNotes
  58    let note: RegExpExecArray | null;
  59    while ((note = noteRe.exec(text))) {
  60      const line = text.slice(0, note.index).split('\n').length - 1;
  61      const scene = [...scenes].reverse().find((s) => s.line <= line);
  62      if (!scene) continue;
  63      const tagRe = /@([A-Za-z][\w-]*)\s*:\s*([^@]+)/g;
  64      let tag: RegExpExecArray | null;
  65      while ((tag = tagRe.exec(note[1]))) {
  66        const category = tag[1].toLowerCase();
  67        const items = tag[2]
  68          .split(',')
  69          .map((s) => s.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim())
  70          .filter(Boolean);
  71        if (items.length) (scene.tags[category] ??= []).push(...items);
  72      }
  73    }
  74  }
  75  
  76  export function buildBreakdown(text: string): Breakdown {
  77    const doc = parse(text);
  78    const els = doc.elements;
  79    const sceneIdxs = els.flatMap((e, i) => (e.kind === 'scene' ? [i] : []));
  80    const scenes: SceneBreakdown[] = [];
  81  
  82    for (let s = 0; s < sceneIdxs.length; s++) {
  83      const start = sceneIdxs[s];
  84      const end = s + 1 < sceneIdxs.length ? sceneIdxs[s + 1] : els.length;
  85      const heading = els[start] as SceneHeading;
  86      const slice = els.slice(start, end);
  87  
  88      const characters: string[] = [];
  89      for (const el of slice) {
  90        if (el.kind !== 'dialogue') continue;
  91        const name = el.character.replace(/\s*\(.*\)\s*$/, '').toUpperCase();
  92        if (name && !characters.includes(name)) characters.push(name);
  93      }
  94  
  95      // Reuse the PDF layout so eighths match the printed page exactly.
  96      const lineCount = layout({ frontmatter: {}, elements: slice }).length;
  97  
  98      scenes.push({
  99        number: heading.number,
 100        slug: heading.text.toUpperCase(),
 101        ...parseSlug(heading.text),
 102        characters,
 103        eighths: Math.max(1, Math.round(lineCount / LINES_PER_EIGHTH)),
 104        tags: {},
 105        line: heading.line,
 106      });
 107    }
 108  
 109    collectTags(text, scenes);
 110  
 111    const characters = [...new Set(scenes.flatMap((s) => s.characters))];
 112    const locations = [...new Set(scenes.map((s) => s.location))];
 113    return {
 114      scenes,
 115      characters,
 116      locations,
 117      totalEighths: scenes.reduce((sum, s) => sum + s.eighths, 0),
 118    };
 119  }
 120  
 121  function csvField(value: string): string {
 122    // Leading apostrophe defuses spreadsheet formula injection (=, +, -, @ starters).
 123    const safe = /^[=+@-]/.test(value) ? `'${value}` : value;
 124    return /[",\n]/.test(safe) ? `"${safe.replace(/"/g, '""')}"` : safe;
 125  }
 126  
 127  const flatTags = (tags: Record<string, string[]>): string =>
 128    Object.entries(tags)
 129      .map(([cat, items]) => `${cat}: ${items.join(', ')}`)
 130      .join('; ');
 131  
 132  export function breakdownToMarkdown(bd: Breakdown, title: string): string {
 133    const out: string[] = [
 134      `# Scene Breakdown — ${title}`,
 135      '',
 136      `Total: ${bd.scenes.length} scenes, ${formatEighths(bd.totalEighths)} pgs`,
 137      '',
 138      '| # | Slug | I/E | Location | Time | Pages | Cast | Elements |',
 139      '|---|------|-----|----------|------|-------|------|----------|',
 140    ];
 141    for (const s of bd.scenes) {
 142      out.push(
 143        `| ${s.number ?? ''} | ${s.slug} | ${s.intExt} | ${s.location} | ${s.timeOfDay} | ${formatEighths(s.eighths)} | ${s.characters.join(', ')} | ${flatTags(s.tags)} |`
 144      );
 145    }
 146  
 147    out.push('', '## Cast', '');
 148    for (const name of bd.characters) {
 149      const appears = bd.scenes.filter((s) => s.characters.includes(name));
 150      const nums = appears.map((s) => s.number ?? `@${s.line + 1}`).join(', ');
 151      out.push(`- **${name}** — ${appears.length} scene${appears.length === 1 ? '' : 's'} (${nums})`);
 152    }
 153  
 154    out.push('', '## Locations', '');
 155    for (const loc of bd.locations) {
 156      const at = bd.scenes.filter((s) => s.location === loc);
 157      const eighths = at.reduce((sum, s) => sum + s.eighths, 0);
 158      out.push(`- **${loc}** — ${at.length} scene${at.length === 1 ? '' : 's'}, ${formatEighths(eighths)} pgs`);
 159    }
 160  
 161    return out.join('\n') + '\n';
 162  }
 163  
 164  export function breakdownToCsv(bd: Breakdown): string {
 165    const rows = [['Scene', 'Slug', 'IntExt', 'Location', 'Time', 'Eighths', 'Cast', 'Elements']];
 166    for (const s of bd.scenes) {
 167      rows.push([
 168        s.number ?? '',
 169        s.slug,
 170        s.intExt,
 171        s.location,
 172        s.timeOfDay,
 173        String(s.eighths),
 174        s.characters.join(', '),
 175        flatTags(s.tags),
 176      ]);
 177    }
 178    return rows.map((r) => r.map(csvField).join(',')).join('\n') + '\n';
 179  }

  10    lines: BudgetLine[];

  15  export interface Budget {
  16    sections: BudgetSection[];
  17    estimate: number;

  20  
  21  const TOTALS_HEADING = '## Totals';
  22  const GENERATED_MARK = '<!-- generated by ScreenMark — edits here are overwritten -->';
  23  const GENERATED_END = '<!-- /screenmark-totals -->';
  24  
  25  function parseMoney(cell: string): number | null {
  26    const cleaned = cell.replace(/[$,\s]/g, '');
  27    if (cleaned === '') return null;
  28    // Strict decimal only — Number() would accept 0x10 / 1e3 and turn typos into money.
  29    if (!/^-?\d+(\.\d+)?$/.test(cleaned)) return null;
  30    return Number(cleaned);
  31  }
  32  
  33  function splitRow(line: string): string[] {
  34    return line
  35      .replace(/^\s*\|/, '')
  36      .replace(/\|\s*$/, '')
  37      .split('|')
  38      .map((c) => c.trim());
  39  }
  40  
  41  const isTableRow = (line: string): boolean => /^\s*\|.*\|\s*$/.test(line);
  42  const isDividerRow = (cells: string[]): boolean => cells.every((c) => /^:?-+:?$/.test(c));
  43  
  44  /** Parse a budget markdown doc: `## Section` headings each followed by a table with Estimate/Actual columns. */
  45  export function parseBudget(md: string): Budget {
  46    const lines = md.split(/\r?\n/);
  47    const sections: BudgetSection[] = [];
  48    let section: BudgetSection | null = null;
  49    let cols: Record<string, number> | null = null;
  50  
  51    for (const line of lines) {
  52      const heading = line.match(/^##\s+(.*)$/);
  53      if (heading) {
  54        const name = heading[1].trim();
  55        cols = null;
  56        if (name.toLowerCase() === 'totals') {
  57          section = null; // never re-ingest our own generated section
  58        } else {
  59          section = { name, lines: [], estimate: 0, actual: 0 };
  60          sections.push(section);
  61        }
  62        continue;
  63      }
  64      if (!section || !isTableRow(line)) continue;
  65      const cells = splitRow(line);
  66      if (isDividerRow(cells)) continue;
  67      if (!cols) {
  68        // Header row: locate columns by name.
  69        const lowered = cells.map((c) => c.toLowerCase());
  70        if (lowered.includes('estimate')) {
  71          cols = {
  72            item: Math.max(0, lowered.findIndex((c) => c === 'item' || c === 'line item')),
  73            estimate: lowered.indexOf('estimate'),
  74            actual: lowered.indexOf('actual'),
  75            notes: lowered.indexOf('notes'),
  76          };
  77        }
  78        continue;
  79      }
  80      const entry: BudgetLine = {
  81        item: cells[cols.item] ?? '',
  82        estimate: cols.estimate >= 0 ? parseMoney(cells[cols.estimate] ?? '') : null,
  83        actual: cols.actual >= 0 ? parseMoney(cells[cols.actual] ?? '') : null,
  84        notes: cols.notes >= 0 ? (cells[cols.notes] ?? '') : '',
  85      };
  86      section.lines.push(entry);
  87      section.estimate += entry.estimate ?? 0;
  88      section.actual += entry.actual ?? 0;
  89    }
  90  
  91    const withTables = sections.filter((s) => s.lines.length > 0);
  92    return {
  93      sections: withTables,
  94      estimate: withTables.reduce((sum, s) => sum + s.estimate, 0),
  95      actual: withTables.reduce((sum, s) => sum + s.actual, 0),
  96    };
  97  }
  98  
  99  const money = (n: number): string => `$${n.toLocaleString('en-US', { maximumFractionDigits: 2 })}`;
 100  
 101  function varianceCell(estimate: number, actual: number): string {
 102    const v = actual - estimate;
 103    if (v === 0) return '—';
 104    return v > 0 ? `+${money(v)} over` : `${money(-v)} under`;
 105  }
 106  
 107  export function renderTotals(budget: Budget): string {
 108    const out: string[] = [
 109      TOTALS_HEADING,
 110      '',
 111      GENERATED_MARK,
 112      '',
 113      '| Section | Estimate | Actual | Variance |',
 114      '|---------|----------|--------|----------|',
 115    ];
 116    for (const s of budget.sections) {
 117      out.push(`| ${s.name} | ${money(s.estimate)} | ${money(s.actual)} | ${varianceCell(s.estimate, s.actual)} |`);
 118    }
 119    out.push(
 120      `| **Total** | **${money(budget.estimate)}** | **${money(budget.actual)}** | **${varianceCell(budget.estimate, budget.actual)}** |`,
 121      GENERATED_END
 122    );
 123    return out.join('\n');
 124  }
 125  
 126  /**
 127   * Replace (or append) the generated `## Totals` block, leaving everything else
 128   * untouched. The block is bounded by GENERATED_END; for blocks written before
 129   * that sentinel existed, fall back to scanning only over the generated shape
 130   * (blank lines, the marker, table rows) so user prose below is never eaten.
 131   */
 132  export function upsertTotals(md: string): string {
 133    const totals = renderTotals(parseBudget(md));
 134    const start = md.search(new RegExp(`^${TOTALS_HEADING}\\s*$`, 'm'));
 135    if (start === -1) {
 136      return md.replace(/\s*$/, '\n\n') + totals + '\n';
 137    }
 138  
 139    let end = md.indexOf(GENERATED_END, start);
 140    if (end !== -1) {
 141      end += GENERATED_END.length;
 142    } else {
 143      end = start + TOTALS_HEADING.length;
 144      for (const lineMatch of md.slice(end).matchAll(/[^\n]*\n?/g)) {
 145        const line = lineMatch[0];
 146        const t = line.trim();
 147        const generatedShape = t === '' || t === GENERATED_MARK || /^\|.*\|$/.test(t);
 148        if (!generatedShape) break;
 149        end += line.length;
 150        if (line.indexOf('\n') === -1) break; // last line of file
 151      }
 152      end = start + md.slice(start, end).replace(/\s+$/, '').length; // don't swallow trailing blank gap
 153    }
 154  
 155    const suffix = md.slice(end).replace(/^\s*\n/, '');
 156    return md.slice(0, start) + totals + (suffix.trim() ? '\n\n' + suffix : '\n');
 157  }

 166        ...rows.map((r) => `| ${r.join(' | ')} |`),
 167        '',
 168      ].join('\n');
 169  
 170    return [
 171      `# Budget — ${title}`,
 172      '',
 173      'Fill in Estimate/Actual (plain numbers or $1,234.56). Run **ScreenMark: Budget Summary** to refresh the Totals section.',
 174      '',

   3  const TITLE_KEYS: Record<string, string> = {
   4    title: 'Title',
   5    credit: 'Credit',
   6    author: 'Author',
   7    authors: 'Authors',
   8    source: 'Source',
   9    draft: 'Draft date',
  10    'draft date': 'Draft date',
  11    date: 'Date',
  12    contact: 'Contact',
  13    copyright: 'Copyright',
  14    notes: 'Notes',
  15  };
  16  
  17  const SLUG_PREFIX_RE = /^(INT|EXT|EST|INT\.?\/EXT|I\/E)[. ]/i;
  18  const ALL_CAPS_RE = /^[^a-z]*$/;
  19  
  20  export function toFountain(doc: ScreenplayDoc): string {
  21    const out: string[] = [];
  22  
  23    const titleEntries = Object.entries(doc.frontmatter);
  24    if (titleEntries.length > 0) {
  25      for (const [key, value] of titleEntries) {
  26        const fountainKey = TITLE_KEYS[key] ?? key.replace(/\b\w/g, (c) => c.toUpperCase());
  27        out.push(`${fountainKey}: ${value}`);
  28      }
  29      out.push('');
  30    }
  31  
  32    for (let i = 0; i < doc.elements.length; i++) {
  33      const el = doc.elements[i];
  34      switch (el.kind) {
  35        case 'section':
  36          out.push('#'.repeat(el.depth) + ' ' + el.text, '');
  37          break;
  38        case 'scene': {
  39          const slug = el.text.toUpperCase();
  40          const forced = SLUG_PREFIX_RE.test(slug) ? slug : '.' + slug;
  41          out.push(forced + (el.number ? ` #${el.number}#` : ''), '');
  42          break;
  43        }
  44        case 'action': {
  45          // Guard only the first line against being misread as a cue/transition —
  46          // interior lines can't be (no preceding blank), and Fountain prints a
  47          // mid-paragraph '!' verbatim.
  48          const lines = el.text.split('\n');
  49          if (ALL_CAPS_RE.test(lines[0]) && /[A-Z]/.test(lines[0])) lines[0] = '!' + lines[0];
  50          out.push(lines.join('\n'), '');
  51          break;
  52        }
  53        case 'dialogue': {
  54          const nameOnly = el.character.replace(/\(.*\)/g, '').trim();
  55          const cue = ALL_CAPS_RE.test(nameOnly) ? el.character : '@' + el.character;
  56          out.push(cue + (el.dual ? ' ^' : ''));
  57          for (const part of el.parts) {
  58            if (part.type === 'parenthetical') out.push(`(${part.text})`);
  59            else if (part.type === 'lyric') out.push('~' + part.text);
  60            else out.push(part.text === '' ? '  ' : part.text);
  61          }
  62          out.push('');
  63          break;
  64        }
  65        case 'transition': {
  66          const text = el.text.toUpperCase();
  67          out.push(/TO:$/.test(text) && ALL_CAPS_RE.test(el.text) ? text : '> ' + text, '');
  68          break;
  69        }
  70        case 'centered':
  71          out.push(`> ${el.text} <`, '');
  72          break;
  73        case 'lyric':
  74          out.push('~' + el.text, '');
  75          break;
  76        case 'pagebreak':
  77          out.push('===', '');
  78          break;
  79      }
  80    }
  81  
  82    while (out.length > 0 && out[out.length - 1] === '') out.pop();
  83    return out.join('\n') + '\n';
  84  }

   4  export const SECTION_RE = /^(#{1,6})\s+(.*)$/;
   5  export const CHARACTER_RE = /^\*\*([^*]+)\*\*\s*(\^)?$/;
   6  export const PARENTHETICAL_RE = /^_\((.*)\)_$/;

  13  /** Blank out `<!-- ... -->` notes while preserving line numbers. */
  14  export function stripNotes(text: string): string {
  15    return text.replace(/<!--[\s\S]*?(-->|$)/g, (m) => m.replace(/[^\n]/g, ''));

  17  
  18  export function parse(text: string): ScreenplayDoc {

  22

  24    if (lines[0]?.trim() === '---') {
  25      let end = -1;

  27        if (lines[j].trim() === '---') {
  28          end = j;
  29          break;
  30        }
  31      }
  32      if (end > 0) {
  33        for (let j = 1; j < end; j++) {
  34          const m = lines[j].match(/^\s*([A-Za-z][\w ]*?)\s*:\s*(.*)$/);
  35          if (m) frontmatter[m[1].toLowerCase()] = m[2].trim();

  37        i = end + 1;
  38      }
  39    }
  40  
  41    let dialogue: Dialogue | null = null;
  42    let action: { lines: string[]; line: number } | null = null;
  43  
  44    const flushAction = () => {
  45      if (action) {
  46        elements.push({ kind: 'action', text: action.lines.join('\n'), line: action.line } as Action);
  47        action = null;
  48      }
  49    };
  50    const appendAction = (text: string, line: number) => {
  51      dialogue = null;
  52      if (action) action.lines.push(text);
  53      else action = { lines: [text], line };
  54    };
  55  
  56    for (; i < lines.length; i++) {

  61        flushAction();
  62        continue;
  63      }

  65      let m: RegExpMatchArray | null;
  66  
  67      if (PAGEBREAK_RE.test(t)) {

  77        flushAction();
  78        elements.push({ kind: 'section', text: m[2].trim(), depth: m[1].length, line: i });
  79      } else if ((m = t.match(CHARACTER_RE))) {
  80        flushAction();
  81        dialogue = { kind: 'dialogue', character: m[1].trim(), dual: m[2] === '^', parts: [], line: i };
  82        elements.push(dialogue);
  83      } else if ((m = t.match(CENTERED_RE))) {
  84        dialogue = null;
  85        flushAction();
  86        elements.push({ kind: 'centered', text: m[1], line: i });
  87      } else if ((m = t.match(DIALOG_RE))) {
  88        if (dialogue) dialogue.parts.push({ type: 'line', text: m[1] });
  89        else appendAction(t, i); // orphan blockquote: fall back to action, keep raw
  90      } else if ((m = t.match(PARENTHETICAL_RE))) {
  91        if (dialogue) dialogue.parts.push({ type: 'parenthetical', text: m[1].trim() });
  92        else appendAction(t, i);
  93      } else if ((m = t.match(LYRIC_RE))) {
  94        if (dialogue) dialogue.parts.push({ type: 'lyric', text: m[1] });
  95        else {
  96          flushAction();
  97          elements.push({ kind: 'lyric', text: m[1], line: i });
  98        }
  99      } else if ((m = t.match(TRANSITION_RE))) {
 100        dialogue = null;
 101        flushAction();
 102        elements.push({ kind: 'transition', text: m[1].trim(), line: i });
 103      } else {
 104        appendAction(t, i);
 105      }
 106    }
 107    flushAction();
 108  
 109    return { frontmatter, elements };
 110  }

  60  export function wrap(text: string, width: number): string[] {
  61    const out: string[] = [];
  62    for (const para of text.split('\n')) {
  63      if (para === '') {
  64        out.push('');
  65        continue;
  66      }
  67      let line = '';
  68      for (const word of para.split(/\s+/)) {
  69        let w = word;
  70        while (w.length > width) {
  71          // hard-split words longer than the column
  72          if (line) {
  73            out.push(line);
  74            line = '';
  75          }
  76          out.push(w.slice(0, width));
  77          w = w.slice(width);
  78        }
  79        if (line === '') line = w;
  80        else if (line.length + 1 + w.length <= width) line += ' ' + w;
  81        else {
  82          out.push(line);
  83          line = w;
  84        }
  85      }
  86      out.push(line);
  87    }
  88    return out;
  89  }
  90  
  91  const blank = (): PLine => ({ spans: [] });

  93  function dialogueLines(el: Dialogue, id: number): PLine[] {

  95    const lines: PLine[] = [];

  97      spans: [{ x: M_LEFT + IND.character * CHAR_W, text: dlg.character }],
  98      keepWithNext: el.parts.length > 0 ? 1 : undefined,

 113    return lines;

 124        }

 128      }
 129    }
 130    return rows;
 131  }

 133  function dualDialogueLines(left: Dialogue, right: Dialogue): PLine[] {
 134    const l = dualColumnRows(left);
 135    const r = dualColumnRows(right);
 136    const lines: PLine[] = [];
 137    for (let i = 0; i < Math.max(l.length, r.length); i++) {
 138      const spans: Span[] = [];
 139      if (l[i]) spans.push({ x: M_LEFT + l[i].indent * CHAR_W, text: l[i].text, font: l[i].font });
 140      if (r[i]) {
 141        spans.push({
 142          x: M_LEFT + (DUAL.rightOffset + r[i].indent) * CHAR_W,
 143          text: r[i].text,
 144          font: r[i].font,
 145        });
 146      }
 147      lines.push({ spans });
 148    }
 149    // Dual blocks have no valid mid-split rendering (two columns would lose both
 150    // cues), so keep the whole block on one page. paginate ignores keeps larger
 151    // than a page, so an absurdly tall block still flows instead of vanishing.
 152    if (lines[0]) lines[0].keepWithNext = lines.length - 1 || undefined;
 153    return lines;

 156  export function layout(doc: ScreenplayDoc): PLine[] {
 157    const lines: PLine[] = [];
 158    const push = (...ls: PLine[]) => lines.push(...ls);
 159    let dlgId = 0;
 160  
 161    for (let i = 0; i < doc.elements.length; i++) {
 162      const el = doc.elements[i];
 163      if (lines.length > 0 && el.kind !== 'pagebreak') {
 164        push(blank());
 165        if (el.kind === 'scene') push(blank());
 166      }
 167      switch (el.kind) {
 168        case 'scene': {
 169          const spans: Span[] = [{ x: M_LEFT, text: el.text.toUpperCase(), font: 'Courier-Bold' }];
 170          if (el.number) {
 171            spans.unshift({ x: SCENE_NUM_LEFT_X, text: el.number, font: 'Courier-Bold' });
 172            spans.push({ x: SCENE_NUM_RIGHT_X, text: el.number, font: 'Courier-Bold' });
 173          }
 174          push({ spans, keepWithNext: 2 });
 175          break;
 176        }
 177        case 'section':
 178          // Structural only — sections organize the outline, not the printed page.
 179          lines.pop(); // drop the spacing blank(s) we just added
 180          if (lines[lines.length - 1]?.spans.length === 0) lines.pop();
 181          break;
 182        case 'action':
 183          for (const l of wrap(el.text, WIDTH.action)) push({ spans: [{ x: M_LEFT, text: l }] });
 184          break;
 185        case 'dialogue': {
 186          const next = doc.elements[i + 1];
 187          if (next?.kind === 'dialogue' && next.dual) {
 188            push(...dualDialogueLines(el, next)); // dual blocks never split with (MORE)
 189            i++;
 190          } else {
 191            push(...dialogueLines(el, dlgId++));
 192          }
 193          break;
 194        }
 195        case 'transition': {
 196          const text = el.text.toUpperCase();
 197          push({ spans: [{ x: Math.max(M_LEFT, PAGE_W - M_RIGHT - text.length * CHAR_W), text }] });
 198          break;
 199        }
 200        case 'centered': {
 201          const x = M_LEFT + Math.max(0, Math.floor((BODY_CHARS - el.text.length) / 2)) * CHAR_W;
 202          push({ spans: [{ x, text: el.text }] });
 203          break;
 204        }
 205        case 'lyric':
 206          for (const l of wrap(el.text, WIDTH.action)) {
 207            push({ spans: [{ x: M_LEFT, text: l, font: 'Courier-Oblique' }] });
 208          }
 209          break;
 210        case 'pagebreak':
 211          push({ spans: [], forceBreak: true });
 212          break;
 213      }
 214    }
 215    return lines;
 216  }
 217  
 218  export function paginate(lines: PLine[]): PLine[][] {
 219    const pages: PLine[][] = [];
 220    let cur: PLine[] = [];
 221    const flush = () => {
 222      if (cur.length > 0) {
 223        pages.push(cur);
 224        cur = [];
 225      }
 226    };
 227    const atCharIndent = (text: string): Span[] => [{ x: M_LEFT + IND.character * CHAR_W, text }];
 228  
 229    for (const line of lines) {
 230      if (line.forceBreak) {
 231        flush();
 232        continue;
 233      }
 234      if (cur.length === 0 && line.spans.length === 0) continue; // no leading blanks
 235      const needed = 1 + (line.keepWithNext ?? 0);
 236      if (cur.length + needed > LINES_PER_PAGE && needed <= LINES_PER_PAGE) {
 237        const prev = cur[cur.length - 1];
 238        if (line.dlg && !line.dlg.cue && prev?.dlg?.id === line.dlg.id) {
 239          // Splitting inside a dialogue block: (MORE) at the bottom, NAME (CONT'D) on top of the next page.
 240          const moved: PLine[] = [];
 241          while (cur.length + 1 > LINES_PER_PAGE) moved.unshift(cur.pop()!); // make room for (MORE)
 242          const newLast = cur[cur.length - 1];
 243          if (newLast?.dlg?.cue && newLast.dlg.id === line.dlg.id) {
 244            moved.unshift(cur.pop()!); // only the cue would remain — move the whole block start instead
 245          } else {
 246            cur.push({ spans: atCharIndent('(MORE)') });
 247          }
 248          flush();
 249          if (!moved[0]?.dlg?.cue) {
 250            cur.push({ spans: atCharIndent(`${line.dlg.character} (CONT'D)`), dlg: { ...line.dlg, cue: true } });
 251          }
 252          cur.push(...moved, line);
 253          continue;
 254        }
 255        flush();
 256      }
 257      cur.push(line);
 258    }
 259    flush();
 260    return pages;
 261  }

 263  function renderTitlePage(pdf: PDFKit.PDFDocument, fm: Record<string, string>): void {
 264    pdf.addPage();
 265    const centered = (text: string, y: number, font: Font = 'Courier') => {
 266      const x = (PAGE_W - text.length * CHAR_W) / 2;
 267      pdf.font(font).fontSize(12).text(text, Math.max(M_LEFT, x), y, { lineBreak: false });
 268    };
 269    let y = PAGE_H / 3;
 270    centered(fm.title.toUpperCase(), y, 'Courier-Bold');
 271    y += 3 * LINE_H;
 272    if (fm.credit) {
 273      centered(fm.credit, y);
 274      y += 2 * LINE_H;
 275    }
 276    const author = fm.author ?? fm.authors;
 277    if (author) centered(author, y);
 278  
 279    let bottomY = PAGE_H - M_BOTTOM - 4 * LINE_H;
 280    for (const key of ['contact', 'copyright']) {
 281      if (fm[key]) {
 282        pdf.font('Courier').fontSize(12).text(fm[key], M_LEFT, bottomY, { lineBreak: false });
 283        bottomY += LINE_H;
 284      }
 285    }
 286    const draft = fm.draft ?? fm['draft date'] ?? fm.date;
 287    if (draft) {
 288      const x = Math.max(M_LEFT, PAGE_W - M_RIGHT - draft.length * CHAR_W);
 289      pdf.font('Courier').fontSize(12).text(draft, x, PAGE_H - M_BOTTOM - 4 * LINE_H, { lineBreak: false });
 290    }
 291  }
 292  
 293  export function toPdf(doc: ScreenplayDoc): Promise<Buffer> {
 294    return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
 295      const pdf = new PDFDocument({ size: 'LETTER', autoFirstPage: false, margin: 0 });
 296      const chunks: Buffer[] = [];
 297      pdf.on('data', (c: Buffer) => chunks.push(c));
 298      pdf.on('end', () => resolve(Buffer.concat(chunks)));
 299      pdf.on('error', reject);
 300  
 301      if (doc.frontmatter.title) renderTitlePage(pdf, doc.frontmatter);
 302  
 303      const pages = paginate(layout(doc));
 304      pages.forEach((page, pageIdx) => {
 305        pdf.addPage();
 306        if (pageIdx > 0) {
 307          const num = `${pageIdx + 1}.`;
 308          pdf
 309            .font('Courier')
 310            .fontSize(12)
 311            .text(num, PAGE_W - M_RIGHT - num.length * CHAR_W, M_TOP - 2 * LINE_H, { lineBreak: false });
 312        }
 313        let y = M_TOP;
 314        for (const line of page) {
 315          for (const span of line.spans) {
 316            pdf.font(span.font ?? 'Courier').fontSize(12).text(span.text, span.x, y, { lineBreak: false });
 317          }
 318          y += LINE_H;
 319        }
 320      });
 321  
 322      pdf.end();
 323    });
 324  }

Reviewed stable location grouping, day/night partition, greedy capacity packing, oversize-scene behavior, and Markdown rendering. Valid normal inputs preserve all scenes and oversized scenes are deliberately scheduled alone. Reproduced CORE-005; schedule inherits CORE-007 estimates. Limitations: only exact NIGHT/DUSK/EVENING/MIDNIGHT values are classified as night; CONTINUOUS/LATER do not inherit prior lighting context.    1  import { Breakdown, SceneBreakdown, formatEighths } from './breakdown';
   2  
   3  export interface ShootDay {
   4    scenes: SceneBreakdown[];
   5    eighths: number;
   6  }
   7  
   8  const NIGHTISH = ['NIGHT', 'DUSK', 'EVENING', 'MIDNIGHT'];
   9  
  10  /**
  11   * Strip-board ordering: group scenes by location (in order of first appearance,
  12   * minimizing company moves), day work before night work within each location,
  13   * then pack greedily into days of `pagesPerDay` pages.
  14   */
  15  export function buildSchedule(bd: Breakdown, pagesPerDay = 5): ShootDay[] {
  16    const strips: SceneBreakdown[] = [];
  17    for (const loc of bd.locations) {
  18      const group = bd.scenes.filter((s) => s.location === loc);
  19      const day = group.filter((s) => !NIGHTISH.includes(s.timeOfDay));
  20      const night = group.filter((s) => NIGHTISH.includes(s.timeOfDay));
  21      strips.push(...day, ...night);
  22    }
  23  
  24    const capacity = Math.max(1, Math.round(pagesPerDay * 8));
  25    const days: ShootDay[] = [];
  26    let cur: ShootDay = { scenes: [], eighths: 0 };
  27    for (const s of strips) {
  28      if (cur.scenes.length > 0 && cur.eighths + s.eighths > capacity) {
  29        days.push(cur);
  30        cur = { scenes: [], eighths: 0 };
  31      }
  32      cur.scenes.push(s);
  33      cur.eighths += s.eighths;
  34    }
  35    if (cur.scenes.length > 0) days.push(cur);
  36    return days;
  37  }
  38  
  39  export function scheduleToMarkdown(days: ShootDay[], title: string, pagesPerDay: number): string {
  40    const out: string[] = [
  41      `# Shooting Schedule — ${title}`,
  42      '',
  43      `${days.reduce((n, d) => n + d.scenes.length, 0)} scenes over ${days.length} day${days.length === 1 ? '' : 's'} (target ${pagesPerDay} pages/day). Scenes grouped by location, day work before night.`,
  44    ];
  45    days.forEach((day, i) => {
  46      out.push('', `## Day ${i + 1} — ${formatEighths(day.eighths)} pgs`, '');
  47      out.push('| # | Slug | I/E | Time | Pages | Cast | Elements |');
  48      out.push('|---|------|-----|------|-------|------|----------|');
  49      for (const s of day.scenes) {
  50        const tags = Object.entries(s.tags)
  51          .map(([cat, items]) => `${cat}: ${items.join(', ')}`)
  52          .join('; ');
  53        out.push(
  54          `| ${s.number ?? ''} | ${s.slug} | ${s.intExt} | ${s.timeOfDay} | ${formatEighths(s.eighths)} | ${s.characters.join(', ')} | ${tags} |`
  55        );
  56      }
  57    });
  58    return out.join('\n') + '\n';
  59  }

  53      await vscode.window.showTextDocument(doc, { preview: true, viewColumn: vscode.ViewColumn.Beside });
  54    } catch (err) {
  55      vscode.window.showErrorMessage(`ScreenMark: Fountain export failed — ${err}`);
  56    }
  57  }
  58  
  59  async function numberScenes(): Promise<void> {
  60    const editor = activeScreenmarkEditor();
  61    if (!editor) return;
  62    const doc = editor.document;
  63  
  64    const used = new Set<number>();
  65    const unnumbered: number[] = [];
  66    // Scan note-stripped lines so `## ...` inside <!-- --> is ignored, like the parser does.
  67    const lines = stripNotes(doc.getText()).split(/\r?\n/);
  68    for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {
  69      const m = lines[i].trim().match(SCENE_RE);
  70      if (!m) continue;
  71      if (m[2]) {
  72        const n = parseInt(m[2], 10);
  73        if (!isNaN(n)) used.add(n);
  74      } else {
  75        unnumbered.push(i);
  76      }
  77    }
  78    if (unnumbered.length === 0) {
  79      vscode.window.showInformationMessage('ScreenMark: all scenes are already numbered.');
  80      return;
  81    }
  82  
  83    let next = 1;
  84    const edit = new vscode.WorkspaceEdit();
  85    for (const lineNo of unnumbered) {
  86      while (used.has(next)) next++;
  87      used.add(next);
  88      const line = doc.lineAt(lineNo);
  89      edit.insert(doc.uri, line.range.end, ` #${next}#`);
  90    }
  91    await vscode.workspace.applyEdit(edit);
  92  }
  93  
  94  function scriptTitle(editor: vscode.TextEditor): string {
  95    const fm = parse(editor.document.getText()).frontmatter;
  96    return fm.title ?? editor.document.uri.path.split('/').pop()!.replace(/(\.screen)?\.(md|smark)$/i, '');
  97  }
  98  
  99  async function writeAndOpen(target: vscode.Uri, content: string): Promise<void> {
 100    await vscode.workspace.fs.writeFile(target, Buffer.from(content, 'utf8'));
 101    const doc = await vscode.workspace.openTextDocument(target);
 102    await vscode.window.showTextDocument(doc, { preview: true, viewColumn: vscode.ViewColumn.Beside });
 103  }
 104  
 105  async function generateBreakdown(): Promise<void> {
 106    const editor = activeScreenmarkEditor();
 107    if (!editor) return;
 108    const bd = buildBreakdown(editor.document.getText());
 109    if (bd.scenes.length === 0) {
 110      vscode.window.showWarningMessage('ScreenMark: no scene headings (## INT. ...) found.');
 111      return;
 112    }
 113    try {
 114      await vscode.workspace.fs.writeFile(

 119    } catch (err) {

 121    }
 122  }
 123  
 124  async function generateSchedule(): Promise<void> {
 125    const editor = activeScreenmarkEditor();

 127    const bd = buildBreakdown(editor.document.getText());
 128    if (bd.scenes.length === 0) {
 129      vscode.window.showWarningMessage('ScreenMark: no scene headings (## INT. ...) found.');
 130      return;
 131    }
 132    const pagesPerDay = vscode.workspace.getConfiguration('screenmark').get<number>('pagesPerDay', 5);
 133    try {

 138    }
 139  }

 141  async function initBudget(): Promise<void> {
 142    const folder = vscode.workspace.workspaceFolders?.[0];
 143    if (!folder) {
 144      vscode.window.showWarningMessage('ScreenMark: open a folder first.');
 145      return;
 146    }
 147    const target = vscode.Uri.joinPath(folder.uri, 'budget.md');
 148    try {
 149      await vscode.workspace.fs.stat(target);
 150    } catch {
 151      const editor = vscode.window.activeTextEditor;
 152      const title =
 153        editor && editor.document.languageId === LANG ? scriptTitle(editor) : folder.name;
 154      await vscode.workspace.fs.writeFile(target, Buffer.from(budgetTemplate(title), 'utf8'));
 155    }
 156    const doc = await vscode.workspace.openTextDocument(target);

 160  async function budgetSummary(): Promise<void> {
 161    const editor = vscode.window.activeTextEditor;
 162    if (!editor || !/\.md$/i.test(editor.document.uri.path) || !/estimate/i.test(editor.document.getText())) {
 163      vscode.window.showWarningMessage('ScreenMark: open a budget markdown file (tables with an Estimate column) first.');
 164      return;
 165    }
 166    const updated = upsertTotals(editor.document.getText());
 167    const fullRange = new vscode.Range(0, 0, editor.document.lineCount, 0);
 168    const edit = new vscode.WorkspaceEdit();
 169    edit.replace(editor.document.uri, fullRange, updated);
 170    await vscode.workspace.applyEdit(edit);
 171  }

 178      vscode.commands.registerCommand('screenmark.numberScenes', numberScenes),
 179      vscode.commands.registerCommand('screenmark.openPreview', () => PreviewPanel.show(context)),

Reviewed source snapshot
   1  import * as vscode from 'vscode';
   2  import { parse } from '../core/parser';
   3  
   4  const TRANSITIONS = ['CUT TO:', 'FADE IN:', 'FADE OUT.', 'FADE TO BLACK.', 'DISSOLVE TO:', 'SMASH CUT TO:', 'MATCH CUT TO:'];
   5  
   6  export class ScreenmarkCompletionProvider implements vscode.CompletionItemProvider {
   7    provideCompletionItems(
   8      document: vscode.TextDocument,
   9      position: vscode.Position
  10    ): vscode.CompletionItem[] | undefined {
  11      const prefix = document.lineAt(position.line).text.slice(0, position.character);
  12      const lineRange = new vscode.Range(position.line, 0, position.line, position.character);
  13  
  14      // **CHAR — suggest known character names
  15      if (/^\*\*?[^*]*$/.test(prefix)) {
  16        const { elements } = parse(document.getText());
  17        const names: string[] = [];
  18        for (const el of elements) {
  19          if (el.kind === 'dialogue' && el.line !== position.line && !names.includes(el.character)) {
  20            names.push(el.character);
  21          }
  22        }
  23        return names.reverse().map((name, idx) => {
  24          const item = new vscode.CompletionItem(name, vscode.CompletionItemKind.User);
  25          item.insertText = `**${name}**\n> `;
  26          item.range = lineRange;
  27          item.sortText = String(idx).padStart(3, '0'); // most recently used first
  28          return item;
  29        });
  30      }
  31  
  32      // ## — suggest INT./EXT. and known sluglines
  33      if (/^##\s*[^#]*$/.test(prefix)) {
  34        const { elements } = parse(document.getText());
  35        const slugs = new Set<string>(['INT. ', 'EXT. ', 'INT./EXT. ']);
  36        for (const el of elements) {
  37          if (el.kind === 'scene' && el.line !== position.line) slugs.add(el.text);
  38        }
  39        return [...slugs].map((slug) => {
  40          const item = new vscode.CompletionItem(slug, vscode.CompletionItemKind.Module);
  41          item.insertText = `## ${slug}`;
  42          item.range = lineRange;
  43          return item;
  44        });
  45      }
  46  
  47      // @ — suggest standard transitions
  48      if (/^@[^@]*$/.test(prefix)) {
  49        return TRANSITIONS.map((t) => {
  50          const item = new vscode.CompletionItem(t, vscode.CompletionItemKind.Keyword);
  51          item.insertText = `@${t}`;
  52          item.range = lineRange;
  53          return item;
  54        });
  55      }
  56  
  57      return undefined;
  58    }
  59  }

   7  
   8  export class PreviewPanel {
   9    private static current: PreviewPanel | undefined;
  10  
  11    private readonly panel: vscode.WebviewPanel;
  12    private readonly disposables: vscode.Disposable[] = [];
  13    private timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
  14    private trackedDoc: vscode.TextDocument | undefined;
  15    private lastRender: { body: string; line: number } | undefined;
  16  
  17    static show(context: vscode.ExtensionContext): void {
  18      const doc = vscode.window.activeTextEditor?.document;
  19      if (PreviewPanel.current) {
  20        PreviewPanel.current.panel.reveal(vscode.ViewColumn.Beside, true);
  21        PreviewPanel.current.update(doc);
  22        return;
  23      }
  24      PreviewPanel.current = new PreviewPanel(context);
  25      PreviewPanel.current.update(doc);
  26    }
  27  
  28    private constructor(context: vscode.ExtensionContext) {
  29      this.panel = vscode.window.createWebviewPanel(
  30        'screenmark.preview',
  31        'Screenplay Preview',
  32        { viewColumn: vscode.ViewColumn.Beside, preserveFocus: true },
  33        { enableScripts: true }
  34      );
  35      // The shell is set exactly once; all further updates go over postMessage so
  36      // the webview never reloads (full html reassignment on each keystroke is
  37      // what made the panel flash and get killed under memory pressure).
  38      this.panel.webview.html = this.shell();
  39      this.panel.webview.onDidReceiveMessage(
  40        (msg) => {
  41          // Sent on every (re)load of the shell — including after the webview was
  42          // discarded while hidden — so always re-send the latest render.
  43          if (msg?.type === 'ready') this.flush();
  44        },
  45        null,
  46        this.disposables
  47      );
  48      this.panel.onDidDispose(() => this.dispose(), null, this.disposables);
  49      vscode.workspace.onDidChangeTextDocument(
  50        (e) => {
  51          if (e.document === this.trackedDoc) this.scheduleUpdate(e.document);
  52        },
  53        null,
  54        this.disposables
  55      );
  56      vscode.window.onDidChangeActiveTextEditor(
  57        (editor) => {
  58          if (editor?.document.languageId === LANG && editor.document !== this.trackedDoc) {
  59            this.update(editor.document);
  60          }
  61        },
  62        null,
  63        this.disposables
  64      );
  65      vscode.window.onDidChangeTextEditorVisibleRanges(
  66        (e) => {
  67          if (e.textEditor.document === this.trackedDoc) {
  68            const line = e.visibleRanges[0]?.start.line;
  69            if (line !== undefined) this.panel.webview.postMessage({ type: 'reveal', line });
  70          }
  71        },
  72        null,
  73        this.disposables
  74      );
  75      context.subscriptions.push(this.panel);
  76    }
  77  
  78    private scheduleUpdate(doc: vscode.TextDocument): void {
  79      if (this.timer) clearTimeout(this.timer);
  80      this.timer = setTimeout(() => this.update(doc), 300);
  81    }
  82  
  83    private topVisibleLine(doc: vscode.TextDocument): number {
  84      const editor = vscode.window.visibleTextEditors.find((e) => e.document === doc);
  85      return editor?.visibleRanges[0]?.start.line ?? 0;
  86    }
  87  
  88    private update(doc: vscode.TextDocument | undefined): void {
  89      if (!doc || doc.languageId !== LANG) return;
  90      this.trackedDoc = doc;
  91      this.panel.title = `Preview: ${doc.uri.path.split('/').pop()}`;
  92      this.lastRender = {
  93        body: toHtml(parse(doc.getText())),
  94        line: this.topVisibleLine(doc),
  95      };
  96      this.flush();
  97    }
  98  
  99    private flush(): void {
 100      // postMessage is dropped while the webview is hidden; lastRender is
 101      // re-flushed by the 'ready' handshake when it comes back.
 102      if (this.lastRender) this.panel.webview.postMessage({ type: 'render', ...this.lastRender });
 103    }
 104  
 105    private shell(): string {
 106      const nonce = randomBytes(16).toString('base64');
 107      return `<!DOCTYPE html>
 108  <html>
 109  <head>
 110  <meta charset="UTF-8">
 111  <meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; script-src 'nonce-${nonce}';">
 112  <style>${SCREENPLAY_CSS}</style>
 113  </head>
 114  <body>
 115  <div id="root"></div>
 116  <script nonce="${nonce}">
 117  (function () {
 118    var vscode = acquireVsCodeApi();
 119    var firstRender = true;
 120    function reveal(line) {
 121      var best = null;
 122      var els = document.querySelectorAll('[data-line]');
 123      for (var i = 0; i < els.length; i++) {
 124        if (Number(els[i].getAttribute('data-line')) <= line) best = els[i];
 125        else break;
 126      }
 127      if (best) best.scrollIntoView({ block: 'start' });
 128      else window.scrollTo(0, 0);
 129    }
 130    window.addEventListener('message', function (e) {
 131      var m = e.data || {};
 132      if (m.type === 'render') {
 133        document.getElementById('root').innerHTML = m.body;
 134        if (firstRender) {
 135          firstRender = false;
 136          if (m.line > 0) reveal(m.line);
 137        }
 138      } else if (m.type === 'reveal') {
 139        reveal(m.line);
 140      }
 141    });
 142    vscode.postMessage({ type: 'ready' });
 143  })();
 144  </script>
 145  </body>
 146  </html>`;
 147    }
 148  
 149    private dispose(): void {
 150      PreviewPanel.current = undefined;
 151      if (this.timer) clearTimeout(this.timer);
 152      for (const d of this.disposables) d.dispose();
 153    }
 154  }

   1  import * as vscode from 'vscode';
   2  
   3  interface Node {
   4    uri: vscode.Uri;
   5    label: string;
   6    icon: vscode.ThemeIcon;
   7    children?: Node[];
   8  }
   9  
  10  /** Sibling docs shown under each script, when they exist on disk. */
  11  const SIBLINGS: { ext: string; label: string; icon: string }[] = [
  12    { ext: '.breakdown.md', label: 'Scene breakdown', icon: 'checklist' },
  13    { ext: '.breakdown.csv', label: 'Breakdown (CSV)', icon: 'table' },
  14    { ext: '.schedule.md', label: 'Shooting schedule', icon: 'calendar' },
  15    { ext: '.pdf', label: 'Screenplay PDF', icon: 'file-pdf' },
  16    { ext: '.fountain', label: 'Fountain export', icon: 'export' },
  17  ];
  18  
  19  export function scriptBase(uri: vscode.Uri): string {
  20    return uri.path.replace(/(\.screen)?\.(md|smark)$/i, '');
  21  }
  22  
  23  async function exists(uri: vscode.Uri): Promise<boolean> {
  24    try {
  25      await vscode.workspace.fs.stat(uri);
  26      return true;
  27    } catch {
  28      return false;
  29    }
  30  }
  31  
  32  export class ProjectTreeProvider implements vscode.TreeDataProvider<Node> {
  33    private readonly emitter = new vscode.EventEmitter<void>();
  34    readonly onDidChangeTreeData = this.emitter.event;
  35  
  36    refresh(): void {
  37      this.emitter.fire();
  38    }
  39  
  40    getTreeItem(node: Node): vscode.TreeItem {
  41      const item = new vscode.TreeItem(
  42        node.label,
  43        node.children ? vscode.TreeItemCollapsibleState.Expanded : vscode.TreeItemCollapsibleState.None
  44      );
  45      item.iconPath = node.icon;
  46      item.resourceUri = node.uri;
  47      item.tooltip = node.uri.fsPath;
  48      item.command = { command: 'vscode.open', title: 'Open', arguments: [node.uri] };
  49      return item;
  50    }
  51  
  52    async getChildren(node?: Node): Promise<Node[]> {
  53      if (node) return node.children ?? [];
  54  
  55      const scripts = await vscode.workspace.findFiles('**/*.{smark,screen.md}', '**/node_modules/**');
  56      scripts.sort((a, b) => a.path.localeCompare(b.path));
  57  
  58      const roots: Node[] = [];
  59      for (const script of scripts) {
  60        const base = scriptBase(script);
  61        const children: Node[] = [];
  62        for (const sib of SIBLINGS) {
  63          const uri = script.with({ path: base + sib.ext });
  64          if (await exists(uri)) {
  65            children.push({ uri, label: sib.label, icon: new vscode.ThemeIcon(sib.icon) });
  66          }
  67        }
  68        roots.push({
  69          uri: script,
  70          label: script.path.split('/').pop()!,
  71          icon: new vscode.ThemeIcon('book'),
  72          children,
  73        });
  74      }
  75  
  76      const budgets = await vscode.workspace.findFiles('**/budget*.md', '**/node_modules/**');
  77      for (const budget of budgets.sort((a, b) => a.path.localeCompare(b.path))) {
  78        roots.push({
  79          uri: budget,
  80          label: budget.path.split('/').pop()!,
  81          icon: new vscode.ThemeIcon('credit-card'),
  82        });
  83      }
  84      return roots;
  85    }
  86  }
  87  
  88  export function registerProjectTree(context: vscode.ExtensionContext): ProjectTreeProvider {
  89    const provider = new ProjectTreeProvider();
  90    const watcher = vscode.workspace.createFileSystemWatcher('**/*.{smark,md,csv,pdf,fountain}');
  91    watcher.onDidCreate(() => provider.refresh());
  92    watcher.onDidDelete(() => provider.refresh());
  93    context.subscriptions.push(
  94      vscode.window.registerTreeDataProvider('screenmarkProject', provider),
  95      vscode.commands.registerCommand('screenmark.refreshProject', () => provider.refresh()),
  96      watcher
  97    );
  98    return provider;
