Reviewed source snapshot
   1  import * as vscode from 'vscode';
   2  import { parse } from '../core/parser';
   3  import { Element } from '../core/ast';
   4  
   5  function lineRange(document: vscode.TextDocument, from: number, to: number): vscode.Range {
   6    return new vscode.Range(from, 0, to, document.lineAt(to).text.length);
   7  }
   8  
   9  /** End line of the block starting at elements[idx]: the line before the next scene/section boundary. */
  10  function blockEnd(elements: Element[], idx: number, lastLine: number, minDepth?: number): number {
  11    for (let j = idx + 1; j < elements.length; j++) {
  12      const el = elements[j];
  13      if (el.kind === 'scene' && minDepth === undefined) return el.line - 1;
  14      if (el.kind === 'section' && (minDepth === undefined || el.depth <= minDepth)) return el.line - 1;
  15    }
  16    return lastLine;
  17  }
  18  
  19  export class ScreenmarkSymbolProvider implements vscode.DocumentSymbolProvider {
  20    provideDocumentSymbols(document: vscode.TextDocument): vscode.DocumentSymbol[] {
  21      const { elements } = parse(document.getText());
  22      const last = document.lineCount - 1;
  23      const root: vscode.DocumentSymbol[] = [];
  24      let currentSection: vscode.DocumentSymbol | undefined;
  25  
  26      for (let i = 0; i < elements.length; i++) {
  27        const el = elements[i];
  28        if (el.kind === 'section') {
  29          const range = lineRange(document, el.line, blockEnd(elements, i, last, el.depth));
  30          const sym = new vscode.DocumentSymbol(el.text, '', vscode.SymbolKind.Namespace, range, lineRange(document, el.line, el.line));
  31          root.push(sym);
  32          currentSection = sym;
  33        } else if (el.kind === 'scene') {
  34          const name = el.number ? `${el.number}. ${el.text}` : el.text;
  35          const range = lineRange(document, el.line, blockEnd(elements, i, last));
  36          const sym = new vscode.DocumentSymbol(name, '', vscode.SymbolKind.Event, range, lineRange(document, el.line, el.line));
  37          if (currentSection && currentSection.range.contains(range.start)) currentSection.children.push(sym);
  38          else root.push(sym);
  39        }
  40      }
  41      return root;
  42    }
  43  }
  44  
  45  export class ScreenmarkFoldingProvider implements vscode.FoldingRangeProvider {
  46    provideFoldingRanges(document: vscode.TextDocument): vscode.FoldingRange[] {
  47      const { elements } = parse(document.getText());
  48      const last = document.lineCount - 1;
  49      const ranges: vscode.FoldingRange[] = [];
  50      for (let i = 0; i < elements.length; i++) {
  51        const el = elements[i];
  52        if (el.kind !== 'scene' && el.kind !== 'section') continue;
  53        const end = blockEnd(elements, i, last, el.kind === 'section' ? el.depth : undefined);
  54        if (end > el.line) ranges.push(new vscode.FoldingRange(el.line, end, vscode.FoldingRangeKind.Region));
  55      }
  56      return ranges;
  57    }
  58  }

  22  });

  34  
  35  test('long speech splits with (MORE) / (CONT\'D)', () => {
  36    const speech = Array.from({ length: 80 }, (_, k) => `> Line ${k} of the speech.`).join('\n');
  37    const pages = paginate(layout(parse(`**MAYA**\n${speech}`)));
  38    assert.ok(pages.length >= 2, 'speech should span pages');
  39    const p1 = lineTexts(pages[0]);
  40    const p2 = lineTexts(pages[1]);
  41    assert.equal(p1[p1.length - 1], '(MORE)');
  42    assert.equal(p2[0], "MAYA (CONT'D)");
  43  });
  44  
  45  test('short dialogue near page bottom moves whole block instead of splitting', () => {

  47    const filler = Array.from({ length: 51 }, (_, k) => `Filler ${k}.`).join('\n\n');
  48    const pages = paginate(layout(parse(`${filler}\n\n**MAYA**\n> One.\n> Two.\n> Three.`)));
  49    const all = pages.map(lineTexts);
  50    const moreCount = all.flat().filter((t) => t === '(MORE)').length;
  51    const contd = all.flat().filter((t) => t.includes("(CONT'D)")).length;

10 / Audit record

Visual evidence and method

Scope and review allocation

The audit began with the current working directory, including ignored generated files and installed dependencies. Git internals were excluded; no Git commands were run, so branch/history/remote status and differences against main were not inspected. A hash inventory, rather than a commit ID, defines this report’s reproducible snapshot.

ReviewerReasoningWork
Astra core specialistHighSix core modules, four test files and three sample/workbook files; semantic regressions and stress measurements.
Astra export specialistHighPDF, HTML, preview, PDF tests and two visual artifacts; rendering, lifecycle, escaping and independent challenge of core/editor findings.
Astra extension specialistMediumNine editor/language/debug configuration files; actual-code command/provider mocks and static contracts.
Astra inventory specialistLowIndependent file hashes, counts, archive CRC, runtime asset and dependency/version correspondence.
Primary agentSynthesis and reviewRemaining 19 project files, build/test baseline, documentation/assets, dependency advisory context, deduplication and HTML verification.

Skills used: pdf:pdf for render-and-inspect evidence and playwright for report review. Source findings include exact line locations and excerpts captured in this standalone file. Scratch reproductions live in /tmp; important outputs and scripts are embedded below so the report does not rely on scratch persistence.

What this audit does not establish

  • No real VS Code/Cursor extension host, minimum-version host, Windows host, remote workspace, virtual filesystem, screen reader, or external Fountain importer was executed.
  • No complete live registry advisory scan was completed. Public advisory checks are targeted, and file hashes are consistency evidence rather than a proof that third-party code is safe.
  • All first-party files have review coverage; dependencies and generated artifacts have explicitly narrower review depth. This is a comprehensive project audit with those limits, not a line-by-line audit of 1,699 third-party files.
